writeup: TIC 340965597 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 8.418963 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 7.23 percent dimming, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The transit signal has a detection significance of 477.0 in the Box Least Squares periodogram, and pixel-level difference imaging confirms a peak signal-to-noise of 92.8, though with a centroid offset of 2.5 arcseconds from the target position. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, a significant data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ substantially in depth, which may point to a true orbital period twice the initially measured value. The automated machine learning screening assigns this target a score of 0.57, indicating moderate confidence in its status as a real eclipsing system.
